title: Formally smooth local maps of complete Noetherian local rings are regular
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m_A)$ and $(B,\mathfrak m_B)$ be Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] local rings which are complete, i.e. $\mathfrak m_A$-adically, resp. $\mathfrak m_B$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], and let $\varphi:A\to B$ be a local homomorphism ($\varphi(\mathfrak m_A)\subseteq\mathfrak m_B$). If $B$ is formally smooth over $A$ for the $\mathfrak m_B$-adic topology [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic], then $\varphi$ is a regular ring map [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]: $\varphi$ is flat and for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset A$, with residue field $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], the fibre ring $B\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is Noetherian and geometrically regular over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Proposition Tag 07PM (proposition-fs-regular, line 12028), implication (4) => (1), and its proof (Proposition 07NQ fs-flat-fibre-fs; Algebra Lemma 032D complete-local-Noetherian-domain-finite-over-regular; Lemmas find-D, descent-fs, lift-derivation-through-fs, degree-p-extension-regular)

proof.text: *Flatness.* $\varphi$ is a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings and $B$ is formally smooth over $A$ for the $\mathfrak m_B$-adic topology, so $\varphi$ is flat and the closed fibre $B/\mathfrak m_AB$ is geometrically regular over $k=A/\mathfrak m_A$ [lem-weil-pbc-fs-adic-flat-geometrically-regular-closed-fibre]. It remains to show, for every prime $\mathfrak p\subset A$, that the fibre ring $B\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is Noetherian and geometrically regular over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]; fix $\mathfrak p$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Proposition Tag 07PM (proposition-fs-regular, line 12028), first sentences: (4) => (2), (3) by Proposition 07NQ (fs-flat-fibre-fs)

proof.text: *Reduction to $A$ a domain and $\mathfrak p=(0)$.* Put $A_1=A/\mathfrak p$, $B_1=B/\mathfrak pB=B\otimes_AA_1$ [def-weil-module-base-change]. As $\varphi$ is local, $\mathfrak pB\subseteq\mathfrak m_B\ne B$, so $A_1$ and $B_1$ are Noetherian local rings, complete for their maximal ideals $\mathfrak m_{A_1}=\mathfrak m_A/\mathfrak p$, $\mathfrak m_{B_1}=\mathfrak m_B/\mathfrak pB$ [lem-weil-pbc-complete-local-quotient], $A_1$ is a domain with fraction field $K_1=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ (the residue field $A_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak pA_{\mathfrak p}$ is the fraction field of $A/\mathfrak p$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]), and the induced map $\varphi_1:A_1\to B_1$ is local. By base change along $A\to A_1$ [lem-weil-pbc-fs-adic-base-change], $B_1$ is formally smooth over $A_1$ for the $\mathfrak m_BB_1=\mathfrak m_{B_1}$-adic topology; hence by [lem-weil-pbc-fs-adic-flat-geometrically-regular-closed-fibre] $\varphi_1$ is flat and its closed fibre $B_1/\mathfrak m_{A_1}B_1=B/\mathfrak m_AB$ is geometrically regular over $k=A_1/\mathfrak m_{A_1}$. Moreover $B\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)\cong(B\otimes_AA_1)\otimes_{A_1}K_1=B_1\otimes_{A_1}K_1$ as $K_1$-algebras (associativity of the tensor product), and for every field extension $L/K_1$, $L\otimes_{K_1}(B_1\otimes_{A_1}K_1)\cong B_1\otimes_{A_1}L$. So it suffices to show: (*) $B_1\otimes_{A_1}L$ is a regular ring [def-weil-regular-scheme] for every finite purely inseparable extension $L/K_1$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension] (with $L=K_1$ this also gives that the fibre ring is Noetherian, a regular ring being Noetherian).

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Proposition Tag 07PM (proposition-fs-regular, line 12028), second paragraph ('By Lemma 07EG (base-change-fs) we may replace A by A/p and B by B/pB')

proof.text: *The coefficient ring $A_0$ and the algebra $C$.* By [lem-weil-pbc-complete-local-domain-finite-over-regular] applied to the complete Noetherian local domain $A_1$ there is a subring $A_0\subseteq A_1$ which is a regular local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_0=\mathfrak m_{A_1}\cap A_0$, $\mathfrak m_0$-adically complete, over which $A_1$ is a finitely generated module, with $A_0/\mathfrak m_0\xrightarrow{\sim}A_1/\mathfrak m_{A_1}=k$, and $A_0\cong k_0[[X_1,\dots,X_d]]$ for a field $k_0$ or $A_0\cong\Lambda[[X_1,\dots,X_d]]$ for a Cohen ring $\Lambda$. The inclusion $\alpha:A_0\to A_1$ is local (as $\mathfrak m_0=\mathfrak m_{A_1}\cap A_0$). The closed fibre $\overline B=B_1/\mathfrak m_{A_1}B_1=B_1\otimes_{A_1}k$ is formally smooth over $k$ for the $\mathfrak m_{\overline B}$-adic topology by base change of $\varphi_1$ along $A_1\to k$ [lem-weil-pbc-fs-adic-base-change] (the image of $\mathfrak m_{B_1}$ in $\overline B$ is its maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_{\overline B}$), and $\varphi_1$ is flat (Step 2). Hence [lem-weil-pbc-fs-adic-lift-over-finite-coefficient-map] gives a Noetherian local ring $(C,\mathfrak m_C)$, $\mathfrak m_C$-adically complete, a local homomorphism $\gamma:A_0\to C$ with $C$ formally smooth over $A_0$ for the $\mathfrak m_C$-adic topology, and a local $\psi:C\to B_1$ with $\psi\gamma=\varphi_1\alpha$, such that $C\otimes_{A_0}A_1\to B_1$, $c\otimes a\mapsto\psi(c)\varphi_1(a)$, is an isomorphism.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Proposition Tag 07PM (proposition-fs-regular, line 12028), third paragraph (Algebra Lemma 032D; Remark 07NS remark-what-does-it-mean; 'completion in the tensor product is not needed as A_0 -> A is finite', Algebra Lemma 00MA)

proof.text: *Reduction to $C\otimes_{A_0}K_0$.* Let $K_0$ be the fraction field of the domain $A_0$, the localization at $W_0=A_0\setminus\{0\}$. $A_1\otimes_{A_0}K_0$ is the localization of $A_1$ at $W_0$ [lem-weil-pbc-localization-base-change], a subring of $K_1$ containing $A_1$ and $K_0$ which is a finite-dimensional $K_0$-vector space (spanned by generators of the $A_0$-module $A_1$) and a domain, hence a field; so it equals $K_1$ and $[K_1:K_0]<\infty$. Let $L/K_1$ be finite purely inseparable; then $L$ is a finite extension of $K_0$, and by Step 3 and associativity $B_1\otimes_{A_1}L\cong(C\otimes_{A_0}A_1)\otimes_{A_1}L\cong C\otimes_{A_0}L\cong L\otimes_{K_0}(C\otimes_{A_0}K_0)$ [def-weil-module-base-change]. If $C\otimes_{A_0}K_0$ is Noetherian and geometrically regular over $K_0$ [def-weil-pbc-g-ring], the right-hand side is a regular ring because $L/K_0$ is a finitely generated (indeed finite) field extension [lem-weil-pbc-geometrically-regular-finitely-generated-extensions]; this is (*). So it suffices to show: (**) $C\otimes_{A_0}K_0$ is Noetherian and $C\otimes_{A_0}L'$ is regular for every finite purely inseparable extension $L'/K_0$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Proposition Tag 07PM (proposition-fs-regular, line 12028), third paragraph, last sentence ('Hence it suffices to show that C (x)_{A_0} K_0 is a geometrically regular algebra over the fraction field K_0 of A_0')

proof.text: *$C$ and $C\otimes_{A_0}K_0$ are regular.* Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fs-adic-flat-geometrically-regular-closed-fibre] to the local homomorphism $\gamma:A_0\to C$ of Noetherian local rings, formally smooth for the $\mathfrak m_C$-adic topology: $\gamma$ is flat and $C/\mathfrak m_0C$ is geometrically regular over $A_0/\mathfrak m_0$, in particular regular (take $k'=A_0/\mathfrak m_0$ in [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]). As $A_0$ is a regular local ring (Step 3), $C$ is regular by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-over-regular-with-regular-fibre]. $C\otimes_{A_0}K_0$ is the localization of $C$ at $\gamma(W_0)$ [lem-weil-pbc-localization-base-change], hence a regular, in particular Noetherian, ring [lem-weil-pbc-localization-of-regular-ring].

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Proposition Tag 07PM (proposition-fs-regular, line 12028), fourth paragraph ('In this case B is a regular ring, see Algebra, Lemma 031E (flat-over-regular-with-regular-fibre). Hence B (x)_A K is a regular ring too')

proof.text: *Characteristic zero.* If $K_0$ has characteristic $0$, the only finite purely inseparable extension of $K_0$ is $K_0$ itself [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension], and $C\otimes_{A_0}K_0$ is regular by Step 5; so (**) holds. This covers the case $A_0\cong\Lambda[[X_1,\dots,X_d]]$ with $\Lambda$ a Cohen ring, for then $K_0\supseteq\Lambda$ has characteristic $0$: $\Lambda$ is a domain with maximal ideal $p\Lambda\ne0$; if $\ell\cdot1=0$ in $\Lambda$ for a prime $\ell$, then $\ell\ne p$ (else $p\Lambda=0$), so $1=a\ell+bp$ with $a,b\in\mathbf Z$ gives $1=bp\in p\Lambda$, a contradiction. Hence from now on $K_0$ has characteristic $p>0$ (and $A_0\cong k_0[[X_1,\dots,X_d]]$ with $\operatorname{char}k_0=p$).

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Proposition Tag 07PM (proposition-fs-regular, line 12028), fourth paragraph ('we win if the characteristic of K is zero') and fifth paragraph, first sentence

proof.text:
*Characteristic $p$: the induction and the ring $A'$.* We show $C\otimes_{A_0}L$ regular for every finite purely inseparable $L/K_0$ by induction on $[L:K_0]$; $[L:K_0]=1$ is Step 5. If $L
e K_0$, [lem-weil-pbc-purely-inseparable-pth-root-tower] gives an intermediate field $K_0\subseteq M\subsetneq L$, finite purely inseparable over $K_0$ with $[M:K_0]<[L:K_0]$, and $ eta\in L$ with $L=M( eta)$, $g= eta^p\in M$ not a $p$-th power in $M$, $L\cong M[z]/(z^p-g)$. By induction $C\otimes_{A_0}M$ is regular. Choose a $K_0$-basis $m_1,\dots,m_r$ of $M$; each $m_i^{q_i}\in K_0$ for some power $q_i$ of $p$, say $m_i^{q_i}=a_i/s_i$ with $a_i,s_i\in A_0$, $s_i
e0$; then $(s_im_i)^{q_i}=s_i^{q_i-1}a_i\in A_0$, so $s_im_i$ is integral over $A_0$, and $A'=A_0[s_1m_1,\dots,s_rm_r]\subseteq M$ is a domain, a finitely generated $A_0$-module (finitely many integral generators), with fraction field $M$ (it contains $K_0$-multiples generating $M$ and $K_0=\mathrm{Frac}(A_0)$). Write $g=c/e$ with $c,e\in A'$, $e
e0$, and put $f=e^pg=e^{p-1}c\in A'$, $ eta'=e eta$: then $ eta'^p=f$, $L=M( eta')$, $f$ is not a $p$-th power in $M$ (else $g$ would be), and $L\cong M[z]/(z^p-f)$ ($z^p-f$ has the root $ eta'$ and degree $p=[L:M]$). This is 'clearing denominators, we may assume $f\in A'$'.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Proposition Tag 07PM (proposition-fs-regular, line 12028), fifth paragraph ('We will show by induction on [L : K] ... Let A' be a finite A-subalgebra of M with fraction field M. Clearing denominators, we may and do assume f in A'')

proof.text: *A derivation with $D(f)$ a unit.* $A'$ is a domain with $p\cdot1=0$, $f\in A'$ is not a $p$-th power in its fraction field $M$, and $A'$ is a finitely generated $A_0$-module, hence a finite type algebra over the complete Noetherian local ring $A_0$; so [lem-weil-pbc-derivation-nonzero-on-non-pth-power] gives a derivation $D:A'\to A'$ with $D(f)\ne0$. Let $C'=C\otimes_{A_0}A'$ [def-weil-module-base-change]. By base change of $\gamma$ along $A_0\to A'$ [lem-weil-pbc-fs-adic-base-change], $C'$ is formally smooth over $A'$ for the $\mathfrak m_CC'$-adic topology. $C'$ is a finitely generated $C$-module (generated by $1\otimes e_j$ for generators $e_j$ of the $A_0$-module $A'$), and $C$ is Noetherian and $\mathfrak m_C$-adically complete, so $C'\to\varprojlim_nC'/\mathfrak m_C^nC'$ is bijective [lem-weil-pbc-finite-module-complete-over-complete-noetherian]; as $(\mathfrak m_CC')^n=\mathfrak m_C^nC'$, $C'$ is $\mathfrak m_CC'$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. By [lem-weil-pbc-fs-adic-lift-derivation] there is a derivation $D':C'\to C'$ with $D'(1\otimes a)=1\otimes D(a)$ for $a\in A'$. Let $W=A'\setminus\{0\}$; $M=W^{-1}A'$, and $R_M:=C\otimes_{A_0}M\cong C'\otimes_{A'}M$ is the localization of $C'$ at the image $W'$ of $W$ [lem-weil-pbc-localization-base-change]. By [lem-weil-pbc-derivation-extends](2), $D'$ extends to a derivation $D''$ of $W'^{-1}C'\cong R_M$ with $D''(x/1)=D'(x)/1$. Then $D''(f)$ is the image of $D(f)\in W$, a unit of $R_M$. (The source cites Lemma 07EH descent-fs here; the needed statement is the base change Lemma 07EG.)

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Proposition Tag 07PM (proposition-fs-regular, line 12028), fifth paragraph ('By Lemma 07PH (find-D) ... As A' -> B (x)_A A' is formally smooth ... by Lemma 07EH (descent-fs) [read: 07EG base-change-fs] we can use Lemma 07PL (lift-derivation-through-fs) to extend D to D' ... D'(f) = D(f) is a unit in B (x)_A M')

proof.text: *Conclusion of the induction and of the proof.* $R_M=C\otimes_{A_0}M$ is regular (induction hypothesis), $f\in R_M$ and $D''(f)$ is a unit (Step 8), so $R_M[z]/(z^p-f)$ is regular [lem-weil-pbc-degree-p-extension-regular]. Since $L\cong M[z]/(z^p-f)$ (Step 7), $C\otimes_{A_0}L\cong R_M\otimes_ML\cong R_M[z]/(z^p-f)$ [def-weil-module-base-change] (tensoring the presentation over $M$ with $R_M$). This completes the induction, so (**) holds also in characteristic $p$. By Steps 4 and 2, $B\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is Noetherian and geometrically regular over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ for every prime $\mathfrak p$; with the flatness of Step 1, $\varphi$ is a regular ring map [def-weil-pbc-g-ring].

split_report.summary: Statement checked against Stacks 07PM (4) => (1) (kept; the hypothesis uses def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic, R discrete, which for a local map agrees with Definition 07NI by Lemma 07EC(2)). Proof split into 9 steps following the proof of 07PM: flatness and the closed fibre (07NQ); reduction to A a domain, p = 0 (07EG, Algebra 0325); A_0 from Algebra 032D and C from Remark 07NS/Lemma 07NR (no completion since A_0 -> A finite); reduction to C (x) K_0 via Algebra 0381 (finite extension K/K_0); C regular by 07NQ + Algebra 031E and its localization; characteristic 0 case (Cohen ring case has characteristic 0, written out); characteristic p induction on [L:K_0] via the p-th root tower (Fields 09HI), the finite subalgebra A' and clearing denominators written out; derivation by find-D 07PH, base change 07EG, completeness of the finite C-module C' (Algebra 00MA), 07PL, extension to the localization (07PE); conclusion by 07PG. Source error: 07PM cites Lemma 07EH (descent-fs) for 'A' -> B (x)_A A' formally smooth', which is the base change Lemma 07EG. Lemma 07PL is stated for local maps of Noetherian local rings while 07PM applies it to A' -> B (x)_A A' without checking locality; the new node lem-weil-pbc-fs-adic-lift-derivation states it with the hypotheses its proof uses (S n-adically complete), which C' satisfies. 7 new unsplit nodes (07NQ (3)=>(1), 07EG, 07NS(3)(4), 07PL generalized, 07PG, 07PH, Fields 09HI), none in Mathlib (Mathlib has only discrete Algebra.FormallySmooth, no adic formal smoothness, geometric regularity, Cohen structure, or derivation criteria for regularity); reused 10 existing nodes (032D, 0381, 031E, 0325, 00MA finite-module completeness, 07PE, localization lemmas).
